summary: Setup is a Google Cloud project, Gmail API enablement, an OAuth consent screen, a Web application OAuth client, and the exact redirect URI. The catch is that Gmail read/write scopes are restricted, so real users usually hit verification and testing limits.
difficultyReason: Gmail read/write scopes are restricted, and Google says restricted-scope verification can take about 6 weeks; if your app can access restricted Gmail data from or through a server, Google also requires an annual security assessment.

costs.text: Standard Gmail API use has no additional cost.

requirements.text: Create or select a Google Cloud project and enable the Gmail API.
Configure the OAuth consent screen before you create client credentials.
requirements.quote: The OAuth Consent Screen tells users which app is requesting access to their data

requirements.text: If your users are outside your Google Workspace organization, set user type to External.
requirements.quote: available to any user with a Google Account.

requirements.text: Add authorized domains for your home page, privacy policy, terms of service, redirect URIs, and JavaScript origins.
Link a privacy policy from the OAuth consent screen.
requirements.quote: The Privacy Policy must be linked

requirements.text: Create a Web application OAuth client and register redirect URIs that exactly match your callback.
If you keep the app in Testing, add each tester as a test user.
requirements.quote: limited to up to 100 test users

reviewTriggers.text: Requesting gmail.send is sensitive. The main read/write Gmail scopes are restricted, including gmail.readonly, gmail.compose, gmail.insert, gmail.modify, gmail.metadata, gmail.settings.basic, gmail.settings.sharing, and mail.google.com.
reviewTriggers.quote: Read, compose, and send emails from your Gmail account.

reviewTriggers.text: If your app can access restricted Gmail data from or through a server, Google requires an annual security assessment.
External apps in Testing are capped at 100 test users, and test authorizations expire after 7 days.
reviewTriggers.quote: expire seven days from the time of consent.

steps.title: Choose the smallest scope set
steps.detail: For a Gmail agent that reads and writes mail, start with gmail.modify. Add gmail.send only if you want a separate send-only path. Do not request mail.google.com unless you truly need permanent delete or IMAP or SMTP style full access.
steps.quote: Read, compose, and send emails from your Gmail account.

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project
steps.detail: Create or select the project that will own the OAuth app and Gmail API credentials.
steps.quote: it must have a corresponding Google Cloud project

steps.title: Enable the Gmail API
steps.detail: In Google Cloud Console, open API Library and enable the Gmail API for the project.

steps.title: Configure OAuth consent screen
steps.detail: Set app name, support email, user type, privacy policy, terms, authorized domains, and the scopes you will request. Add test users if you stay in Testing.
steps.quote: The OAuth Consent Screen tells users which app is requesting access to their data

steps.title: Create OAuth client credentials
steps.detail: Create an OAuth client ID as a Web application. Put the exact redirect URI from your Composio auth config into the Google client settings, and add any authorized JavaScript origins if your app needs them.

steps.title: Test with listed users only
steps.detail: Keep the app in Testing while you verify the flow. Add each tester to the test users list first, and remember that testing authorizations expire after 7 days.
steps.quote: expire seven days from the time of consent.

steps.title: Submit for verification
steps.detail: Move the app to production, then submit the consent screen for branding verification and the required scope verification. If the app can access restricted Gmail data from or through a server, expect a security assessment step.

steps.title: Wait for approval
steps.detail: Google reviews branding, scopes, and any security assessment work before real users can connect.

steps.title: Publish and onboard real users
steps.detail: After approval, switch the app to production and let real Gmail users connect with the approved scopes.

blockers.problem: If your redirect URI does not match exactly, Google returns redirect_uri_mismatch.
blockers.whatToDo: Copy the exact redirect URI from Composio into the Google OAuth client and keep the scheme, host, port, and path identical.

blockers.problem: Testing mode only allows a small tester set and the authorization expires after 7 days.
blockers.whatToDo: Use Testing only for development, then move to production before onboarding real users.
blockers.quote: limited to up to 100 test users

blockers.problem: Unapproved sensitive or restricted scopes can show the unverified app screen and exhaust the user cap.
blockers.whatToDo: Submit the exact scopes you need for verification before you ask real users to connect.

agentDrafts.title: App description
agentDrafts.text: Our app is an AI assistant that reads a user's Gmail, drafts replies, sends messages they approve, and updates mail state on their behalf.

agentDrafts.title: gmail.modify justification
agentDrafts.text: We request gmail.modify because the agent must read messages, compose drafts, and send mail inside Gmail for the user.

agentDrafts.title: gmail.send justification
agentDrafts.text: We request gmail.send only if we need a separate send-only path or want the narrowest possible sending scope.

openQuestions: What exact redirect URI does Composio show in your auth config?
Do you need only inbox read and write, or also labels, filters, or other Gmail settings?
Will your app store or transmit Gmail data from its servers, which decides whether a security assessment applies?
Are you building for consumer Gmail users outside your organization, or only for a Google Workspace internal audience?
